text.title: Google Performance Max Core Rules
text.summary: 20 testable rules grounding the google-pmax methodology — the 30-conversion floor, 3+ asset groups, audience signals, brand negatives, value priority, then campaign creation (PAUSED first, account-level goals, asset minimums, HTTPS final URLs, upload-then-link), audience and bidding (customer-match primary, 14 days / 30 conversions before targets, 3x CPA budget, label-lagged asset refresh) and API discipline (customer_id format, MCC header, pinned API version, budget micros, validated conversion action). Each rule pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale.

section.title: Rule set

rule.statement: PMax MUST NOT be enabled below 30 conversions/month at the account level.
rule.rationale: PMax requires conversion signal to optimize; below 30/mo it wastes spend in unobservable buckets.

rule.statement: Each PMax campaign MUST have ≥3 asset groups partitioned by theme (audience or product line).
rule.rationale: Single asset group makes Google's blender opaque + un-diagnosable.

rule.statement: Each asset group MUST attach audience signals (custom segments + customer match + remarketing) for cold-start acceleration.
rule.rationale: Without signals PMax explores broadly; with signals it converges in 1-2 weeks instead of 4-6.

rule.statement: Brand keywords MUST be added as account-level negatives on PMax to prevent cannibalization of brand Search campaigns.
rule.rationale: Otherwise PMax shows up on brand queries at higher CPA than dedicated brand Search.

rule.statement: Conversion events used by PMax MUST be assigned value priority (Purchase > Lead > SignUp) or all-or-nothing primary event marking.
rule.rationale: Equal-weight events skew toward low-value conversions.

section.p: Creating a Performance Max campaign via the Google Ads API, setting up asset groups, and meeting minimum asset count requirements before submission.

rule.statement: Always create PMax campaigns with status PAUSED; require explicit human approval before enabling.

rationale.source: Google Ads API campaign status docs

rule.rationale: PMax starts spending immediately upon enable. A paused-first approach gives time to validate asset counts, conversion goals, and URL expansion settings before budget flows.

rule.statement: Configure conversion goals at the account level before creating a PMax campaign; PMax silently optimizes for the wrong action if account-level goals are not set correctly.

rationale.source: Google Ads PMax conversion goals docs

rule.rationale: Unlike Search campaigns that can target specific conversion actions, PMax uses account-level conversion goals. Wrong goals produce campaigns that optimize for micro-conversions (e.g., page views) instead of purchases.

rule.statement: Validate minimum asset counts before submitting an asset group: 5 headlines (30 chars), 5 long headlines (90 chars), 4 descriptions (90 chars), 4 marketing images. Campaigns go nowhere without meeting minimums.
rule.rationale: PMax campaigns with fewer than the minimum asset counts per type cannot enter the auction for placements that require those assets. The campaign runs but delivers zero impressions on major inventory.

rule.statement: final_urls must use HTTPS; HTTP URLs fail with a generic auth error that does not indicate the scheme problem.
rule.rationale: Google requires HTTPS for all ad destination URLs. The error message for HTTP URLs is misleading, making this a time-consuming bug to diagnose.

rule.statement: Upload image assets first via mutate_assets, then reference their resource names in asset group asset operations; assets and asset groups cannot be created in the same API call.
rule.rationale: Asset resources must exist before they can be linked to an asset group. Agents that attempt to create and link in one step receive resource-not-found errors.

section.p: Adding audience signals, bidding strategy progression from Maximize Conversions to Target CPA/ROAS, learning phase rules, and asset refresh cadence.

rule.statement: Use your best-converting customer-match list as the primary audience signal; generic interest segments are much less effective at guiding PMax's optimizer.

rationale.source: Google Ads PMax audience signals docs

rule.rationale: PMax weights converter-similarity heavily. A customer-match list of actual buyers gives the optimizer strong signal. Interest segments give broad demographic hints that PMax often ignores.

rule.statement: Run Maximize Conversions without a target for at least 14 days and 30+ conversions; then switch to Target CPA or Target ROAS.
rule.rationale: Setting a target CPA/ROAS before sufficient data forces the bidder to over-fit on sparse conversions. The learning phase needs unconstrained data collection to train the model.

rule.statement: Keep daily budget at minimum 3x target CPA; below this, PMax stalls on auction-bidding constraints and cannot exit learning.
rule.rationale: PMax needs budget headroom to explore inventory and conversion paths. A budget too close to the target CPA eliminates any exploration margin and traps the campaign in learning indefinitely.

rule.statement: Replace LOW-labeled assets at least quarterly; do not trigger creative swap on performance labels under 7 days old since labels lag 7-14 days.

rationale.source: Google Ads asset performance labels docs

rule.rationale: Asset performance labels have a 7-14 day lag. Swapping assets on day 3 based on PENDING or early LOW labels churns creative unnecessarily and disrupts the optimizer's learning.

rule.statement: Add account-level negative keywords for brand terms to prevent PMax from cannibalizing branded Search campaigns.
rule.rationale: PMax and branded Search campaigns compete in the same auction. Without brand exclusions, PMax steals credit for high-intent branded queries at higher cost than a dedicated Search campaign.

section.p: Google Ads API-specific failure modes for Performance Max campaigns, including enums, customer_id format, and multi-account considerations.

rule.statement: customer_id must be provided as an unhyphenated 10-digit string (e.g., "1234567890"); the hyphenated form from the UI ("123-456-7890") causes authentication errors.
rule.rationale: The Google Ads API does not accept hyphenated customer IDs. Agents that copy-paste from the UI clipboard will silently fail with confusing auth-related error messages.

rule.statement: MCC accounts require the login-customer-id header set to the MCC account ID in the API client; omitting it causes 401 errors on all child account calls.
rule.rationale: Multi-account agents accessing child accounts must authenticate through the MCC. Without the login-customer-id header, calls fail at the authentication layer before reaching the campaign logic.

rule.statement: Pin the Google Ads API version and refresh client stubs when bumping versions; asset field type enums change across versions (e.g., MARKETING_IMAGE vs LANDSCAPE_LOGO naming).
rule.rationale: PMax asset type enums are updated as Google adds new asset types. An agent using enum values from a deprecated version will receive INVALID_ARGUMENT errors that do not name the changed field.

rule.statement: PMax budget amount_micros uses Google Ads conventions: $50/day = 50,000,000 micros (multiply by 1,000,000). LinkedIn costs are decimal floats — do not mix unit systems across platforms.
rule.rationale: Agents working across Google and LinkedIn in the same session commonly apply the wrong unit convention. $50 submitted as 50 to Google Ads creates a $0.000050/day budget that generates zero impressions.

rule.statement: Before creating a PMax campaign, validate that at least one conversion action with include_in_conversions_metric=True exists at the account level and has received conversions in the last 30 days.

rationale.source: Google Ads PMax conversion goals docs

rule.rationale: PMax silently optimizes for the best available conversion action. If the account has no active conversion actions, or only micro-conversions, the campaign will optimize for meaningless events.
